changes.new: ### RedPajama: a reproduction recipe and an annotated web pool RedPajama V1 follows the seven-source recipe described for the first LLaMA: Common Crawl, C4, GitHub, books, arXiv, Wikipedia and Stack Exchange. Its [pinned README](https://github.com/togethercomputer/RedPajama-Data/blob/45b37c2a1d1e495b0f48549ef3ce03ff029f7881/README.md) reports about 1.2 trillion tokens. Reproducing the recipe does not recover Meta's exact documents, filtering decisions or training order. The model-specific sampling fractions and repeated passes are explained in [[02 Areas/ML & DL/00 Учебник/07 Анатомия современной LLM/01 LLaMA как базовая архитектура#Данные и объём предобучения|the LLaMA chapter]]. V2 changes the collection: it processes 84 Common Crawl snapshots in English, French, German, Italian and Spanish. The [release announcement](https://www.together.ai/blog/redpajama-data-v2) describes over 100 trillion raw tokens and more than 40 precomputed quality signals for a smaller annotated subset. These signals let a downstream user select or weight documents; they are not human certificates of correctness. The [dataset card at revision aa033f6](https://huggingface.co/datasets/togethercomputer/RedPajama-Data-V2/blob/aa033f6b6480c445557e9118283993403f069f6a/README.md) separates four components: | Component | What it supplies | | --- | --- | | Documents | Text and source metadata, including snapshot, language and CCNet bucket | | Quality signals | Document- or span-level measurements | | Duplicate IDs | Records to exclude for the released exact-deduplication selection | | MinHash signatures | Features for finding near-duplicate candidates | The published deduplicated `head_middle` subset contains about 20.8 billion documents and an estimated 30.4 trillion tokens. Those counts do not describe every raw document or a fixed model-training budget. The raw files retain duplicates; downloading them and applying a quality threshold does not also apply the separate duplicate-ID list. A constructed example shows the two decisions. Suppose a document passes a length rule but its ID is in the duplicate list: it still has to be excluded from the deduplicated selection. Another document may be unique but fail the length rule. Recomputing one score cannot resolve both cases. Keep the document key consistent across components, apply the selected rules, then count the resulting tokens before choosing a mixture. The MinHash candidate step is developed in [[02 Areas/ML & DL/00 Учебник/11 Pre-training и Scaling/41a Дедупликация, PII и контроль качества корпуса|the deduplication chapter]]. ### ROOTS: language-specific filtering [ROOTS](https://arxiv.org/html/2303.03915v1#S2), used for BLOOM, contains about 1.6 **TB of text**, covering 46 natural and 13 programming languages. Its 62% community-selected / 38% OSCAR split measures bytes, not training-token weights. OSCAR 21.09 was an additional collection path; native speakers set filtering thresholds for 13 of its languages. ![[02 Areas/ML & DL/00 Учебник/Assets/Figures/curated/corpus-releases-2026-10-29/roots-oscar-filtered.png|Original ROOTS Figure 3: documents removed by each filter in five languages]] *Hugo Laurençon and co-authors, [ROOTS, Figure 3](https://arxiv.org/html/2303.03915v1#S3.F3), [CC BY 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Complete original PNG, unchanged. Each bar measures one filter's independent document-removal rate; it is not a successive pipeline stage.* For Simplified Chinese, the seven bars sum to 47%, while all filters together remove 23.1% in Table 1. A document can fail several rules, so adding the bars counts it repeatedly. Perplexity alone removes 18.1% here. The differences across languages reflect their thresholds and inputs; they do not rank the languages' intrinsic text quality. These percentages concern documents, not bytes or tokens. The selected sources, processing tools and component documentation are described in [§§2–4](https://arxiv.org/html/2303.03915v1#S2).
